claims.text: The traceparent header is defined by the W3C Trace Context standard.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (W3C TraceContext is the default ID scheme); ASP.NET Core docs 'Logging' (traceparent header)

claims.text: traceparent is four dash-separated parts: a version ('00'), a 32-hex-digit (16-byte) trace id, a 16-hex-digit (8-byte) parent span id, and flags (e.g. '01').
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (16-byte trace-id, 8-byte span-id); 'Distributed tracing instrumentation walkthroughs' (ParentId output)

claims.text: The parent-id in traceparent is the id of the sender's span that made the request; the receiver uses it as the parent of the span it starts for that request, and keeps the trace id.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (trace-id + parent span-id identify the parent across processes); ASP.NET Core docs 'Logging' (ParentId from inbound traceparent)

claims.text: HttpClient (System.Net.Http) writes a traceparent header on each outgoing request from the span current at that moment; this is on by default. With OpenTelemetry's HttpClient instrumentation on, HttpClient's own span for the call is recorded, and its span id is the one that travels.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (in-box HTTP encode/decode); 'Runtime config: networking' System.Net.Http.EnableActivityPropagation (default true)

claims.text: ASP.NET Core reads an incoming traceparent when it starts the request's Activity: the Activity keeps the header's trace id and has the header's parent-id as its parent span id; the ASP.NET Core instrumentation records it.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs 'Logging and diagnostics' / hosting diagnostics (DistributedContextPropagator); OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore README

claims.text: When a request arrives with no traceparent, the request's span has no parent and a new trace id is generated, so a new trace starts there.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (root Activity gets a new TraceId); W3C Trace Context 'Processing model'

claims.text: Tempo stores and retrieves spans by trace id; spans exported separately by different services with the same trace id form one trace, parent span ids give the tree, times are not used to group them, and Tempo does not merge two trace ids into one trace.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Tempo docs 'Introduction to tracing' / 'Tempo architecture' (traces looked up by trace ID); API GET /api/traces/<traceid>

claims.text: In .NET, Activity.Current is stored per async flow (AsyncLocal), so it follows the code across await; a new Activity started while another is current gets it as parent.
claims.source_hint: .NET API docs System.Diagnostics.Activity.Current ('flows across async calls'); .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts'
